newsitem.title: USA: Divided G7 issues watered-down environment statement.
newsitem.headline: Divided G7 issues watered-down environment statement.

text.p: The Group of Seven summit, split over ways to counter climate change, agreed on Sunday to a watered-down statement on cutting greenhouse gases, European Commision President Jacques Santer said.
U.S. President Bill Clinton held out firmly against an EU plan to set a firm target of a 15 percent cut by the year 2010 in the carbon emissions blamed for global warming, delegates said.
"I am frankly disappointed that not all of our partners were prepared to make quantified commitments on greenhouse gases," Santer said in a statement.
"We have an ambitious position on climate change and will keep pushing for serious cuts."
Delegation officials said that under American pressure the final communique would not even make a non-committal call for "significant cuts" in the noxious gases.
They said Clinton held out until the end and told his partners in the exclusive club of the world's richest nations that G7 members were not supposed to make problems for each other.

The proposal by the G7's European members -- Britain, France, Germany and Italy -- would have committed members to goals that could have required unpopular measures like higher gasoline prices in the U.S.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Sunday the summit was divided into two blocs, with the EU members on one side and the U.S., Japan and Canada on the other.
